scope: Federal law that changes a landlord's or manager's decision in a departing residential tenancy's financial settlement in New York (State and City) and Virginia: debt-collection coverage and conduct at hand-off (FDCPA, Regulation F), servicemember lease termination (SCRA), HUD and USDA program deposit and charge rules that control where inconsistent with state law, Fair Housing Act limits on move-out charges, bankruptcy stay and discharge, FCRA furnisher duties when a balance is reported, and definitions other files depend on (TILA creditor). Stage A legal meaning only. HUD Handbook 4350.3 and the HUD model lease are labeled as guidance and contract form, not regulation.
status: candidate for Owen's review; not accepted. Resolution pass 2026-09-28: zero open questions.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: Any conveying of information regarding a debt to any person, by any medium (letter, itemized statement sent in collection, email, text, call, portal message).
atoms.effect: It is a 'communication'. An itemized balance demand or payment request sent by a debt collector is a communication; the triggers in 1692c, 1692e(11) and 1692g key off it.
atoms.quote: The term "communication" means the conveying of information regarding a debt directly or indirectly to any person through any medium.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: A natural person is obligated, or alleged to be obligated, to pay the balance (tenant, co-tenant, or individual guarantor).
atoms.effect: That person is a 'consumer'. A business entity tenant is not, so a balance owed by a company lessee is outside the FDCPA and Regulation F.
atoms.quote: The term "consumer" means any natural person obligated or allegedly obligated to pay any debt.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: The balance is owed to the person (the landlord/owner, or a successor owner that took the lease). Exception: a person who receives an assignment or transfer of an account already in default solely to collect it for another.
atoms.effect: The owner is the 'creditor'. A creditor collecting its own debt in its own name is not a debt collector (see US:15USC1692a(6)-regularly-another and US:CASE-Henson-2017). An agency that takes a defaulted account only to collect for the owner is not a creditor.
atoms.quote: The term "creditor" means any person who offers or extends credit creating a debt or to whom a debt is owed, but such term does not include any person to the extent that he receives an assignment or transfer of a debt in default solely for the purpose of facilitating collection of such debt for another.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: A consumer's obligation (or alleged obligation) to pay money arises out of a transaction whose subject is primarily for personal, family or household purposes; a residential lease is such a transaction.
atoms.effect: The balance is a 'debt', whether or not reduced to judgment. Rent is a debt (US:CASE-Romea-1998), and so is every other obligation the tenant owes under the lease, including move-out damage, cleaning and fee charges, in both forums (US:15USC1692a(5)-lease-charges). A tort claim against a non-party to the lease is not the non-party's debt (US:15USC1692a(5)-non-party-tort).
judgment_terms: primarily for personal, family, or household purposes
atoms.quote: The term "debt" means any obligation or alleged obligation of a consumer to pay money arising out of a transaction in which the money, property, insurance, or services which are the subject of the transaction are primarily for personal, family, or household purposes, whether or not such obligation has been reduced to judgment.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1986-07-09 (Pub. L. 99-361 wording of par. (6)); in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: any person (collection agency; Handoff if its business is collection)
atoms.condition: The person uses the mails or any instrumentality of interstate commerce (phone, email, internet) in any business whose principal purpose is the collection of any debts.
atoms.effect: The person is a 'debt collector' unless an exclusion in (A)-(F) covers the activity. A collection agency receiving a hand-off is a debt collector under this clause. Henson decided only the second clause; a business whose principal purpose is collecting debts is covered by this clause even for debts it owns (US:HANDOFF-config-principal-purpose), while a property manager or settlement service whose business is not principally collection is not.
atoms.quote: The term "debt collector" means any person who uses any instrumentality of interstate commerce or the mails in any business the principal purpose of which is the collection of any debts

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1986-07-09 (Pub. L. 99-361 wording of par. (6)); in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: managing agent; Handoff; landlord's attorney; collection agency
atoms.condition: The person regularly collects or attempts to collect, directly or indirectly, debts owed or due (or asserted to be owed or due) to another, e.g. a managing agent collecting former tenants' balances for owners, or a service collecting for owners.
atoms.effect: The person is a 'debt collector' unless an exclusion covers the activity. 'Another' asks whose account the debt is collected for at the time of collection: an owner collecting its own balances, including a successor owner or a debt buyer collecting for itself, is not covered by this clause (US:CASE-Henson-2017). A landlord collecting its own former tenants' balances in its own name is therefore not a debt collector.
atoms.quote: or who regularly collects or attempts to collect, directly or indirectly, debts owed or due or asserted to be owed or due another.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.condition: A creditor (the landlord/owner), collecting its own former tenants' balances, uses any name other than its own that would indicate a third person is collecting (e.g. letters under a separate 'recovery' or collection-service name, or under Handoff's name when Handoff is not in fact collecting).
atoms.effect: The creditor becomes a 'debt collector' for that collection, even though the (F) exclusions would otherwise apply, and must comply with the FDCPA and Regulation F.
judgment_terms: any name other than his own which would indicate that a third person is collecting
atoms.quote: Notwithstanding the exclusion provided by clause (F) of the last sentence of this paragraph, the term includes any creditor who, in the process of collecting his own debts, uses any name other than his own which would indicate that a third person is collecting or attempting to collect such debts.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: An officer or employee of the creditor (the owner entity) collects the owner's balances in the owner's name.
atoms.effect: Not a debt collector for that activity. The exclusion is for the creditor's own officers and employees; a separate managing company or a vendor such as Handoff is not the creditor's employee and must rely on another exclusion.
atoms.quote: any officer or employee of a creditor while, in the name of the creditor, collecting debts for such creditor;

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: A company collects only for persons related to it by common ownership or corporate control (e.g. an in-house management affiliate of the owner group), and its principal business is not debt collection.
atoms.effect: Not a debt collector while so acting. A manager that also collects for unaffiliated owners loses this exclusion.
atoms.quote: any person while acting as a debt collector for another person, both of whom are related by common ownership or affiliated by corporate control, if the person acting as a debt collector does so only for persons to whom it is so related or affiliated and if the principal business of such person is not the collection of debts;

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: An officer or employee of the United States or a State (a 'State' includes any political subdivision, 1692a(8)) collects in performance of official duties, e.g. PHA staff collecting a former public-housing tenant's charges.
atoms.effect: Not a debt collector for that activity. A New York or Virginia housing authority is a political subdivision, so its officers and employees are within the exclusion (US:15USC1692a(6)(C)-PHA-staff); a private management company running PHA property is not (US:15USC1692a(6)(C)-private-manager).
judgment_terms: officer or employee of ... any State
in the performance of his official duties
atoms.quote: any officer or employee of the United States or any State to the extent that collecting or attempting to collect any debt is in the performance of his official duties;

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: A person collects a debt owed to another, and the collection is incidental to a bona fide fiduciary obligation (e.g. a managing agent's agency duties to the owner) or a bona fide escrow arrangement.
atoms.effect: Not a debt collector 'to the extent' of that activity. A property manager's collection of tenant and former-tenant balances is incidental when collection is not central to, or the primary purpose of, its duties to the owner (US:15USC1692a(6)(F)(i)-manager-incidental); a collection-only engagement is not incidental (US:15USC1692a(6)(F)(i)-collection-only).
atoms.quote: any person collecting or attempting to collect any debt owed or due or asserted to be owed or due another to the extent such activity (i) is incidental to a bona fide fiduciary obligation or a bona fide escrow arrangement;

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: managing agent; Handoff; any servicer engaged before default
atoms.condition: The person collects a debt owed to another, and the debt was not in default when the person obtained it (e.g. the manager held the tenant's account from lease-up; Handoff was engaged on the account at notice or move-out, before any balance was past due).
atoms.effect: Not a debt collector for that debt. A collection agency or attorney that receives the account after it is in default is not excluded by (F)(iii). A move-out balance is not in default when it falls due; it defaults when the lease's delinquency period runs or when the owner treats it as in default (US:15USC1692a(6)(F)(iii)-default-meaning). Application by engagement date: US:15USC1692a(6)(F)(iii)-moveout-branches.
judgment_terms: at the time it was obtained by such person
atoms.quote: (iii) concerns a debt which was not in default at the time it was obtained by such person;

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The former tenant left no forwarding address and the debt collector contacts a third person (neighbor, employer, relative) to find the tenant's home address, phone at that address, or place of employment.
atoms.effect: Identify self and state only that location information is being confirmed; never state the person owes a debt; contact each third person once unless asked or the earlier answer was wrong; no postcards; no collection wording on envelopes; if the consumer has a known attorney, contact only the attorney. Implemented by 12 CFR 1006.10.
judgment_terms: reasonably believes that the earlier response of such person is erroneous or incomplete
atoms.quote: Any debt collector communicating with any person other than the consumer for the purpose of acquiring location information about the consumer shall-

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: Without the consumer's prior consent given directly to the debt collector or a court's express permission.
atoms.effect: No communication at an unusual or known-inconvenient time or place (8 a.m.-9 p.m. local time presumed convenient); none with a consumer known to be represented by an attorney on the debt (unless the attorney fails to respond in a reasonable time or consents); none at work if the employer is known to prohibit it. Reg F 1006.6(b) extends these to attempts to communicate.
atoms.quote: In the absence of knowledge of circumstances to the contrary, a debt collector shall assume that the convenient time for communicating with a consumer is after 8 o'clock antemeridian and before 9 o'clock postmeridian, local time at the consumer's location;

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The debt collector wants to discuss the balance with anyone other than the consumer (e.g. a non-obligated roommate, the new occupant, a relative, the employer).
atoms.effect: Prohibited except with: the consumer, the consumer's attorney, a consumer reporting agency where otherwise permitted, the creditor (owner), the creditor's attorney, or the debt collector's attorney; or with the consumer's direct prior consent, court permission, post-judgment remedy, or for location information under 1692b. Hand-off data flows from owner to collector are communications with 'the creditor' and allowed.
atoms.quote: a debt collector may not communicate, in connection with the collection of any debt, with any person other than the consumer, his attorney, a consumer reporting agency if otherwise permitted by law, the creditor, the attorney of the creditor, or the attorney of the debt collector.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The consumer notifies the debt collector in writing that the consumer refuses to pay or wants communication to stop (complete on receipt if mailed).
atoms.effect: Stop communicating about that debt, except to say efforts are ending, or to notify that the collector or creditor may invoke, or intends to invoke, a specified remedy (e.g. suit). This moves the decision to sue, report, or write off.
atoms.quote: If a consumer notifies a debt collector in writing that the consumer refuses to pay a debt or that the consumer wishes the debt collector to cease further communication with the consumer, the debt collector shall not communicate further with the consumer with respect to such debt, except-

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: Applying 1692c.
atoms.effect: 'Consumer' includes the consumer's spouse, parent (if a minor), guardian, executor or administrator; the collector may discuss the debt with them. Reg F 1006.6(a) adds a confirmed successor in interest and limits executor/administrator to a deceased consumer's estate.
atoms.quote: For the purpose of this section, the term "consumer" includes the consumer's spouse, parent (if the consumer is a minor), guardian, executor, or administrator.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: Any collection conduct toward any person.
atoms.effect: No conduct whose natural consequence is to harass, oppress or abuse; listed examples include threats of violence, obscene language, publishing a list of debtors (other than to a consumer reporting agency), repeated calls with intent to annoy, and calls without meaningful disclosure of identity. Call frequency presumptions in US:12CFR1006.14(b)(2).
judgment_terms: natural consequence of which is to harass, oppress, or abuse
atoms.quote: A debt collector may not engage in any conduct the natural consequence of which is to harass, oppress, or abuse any person in connection with the collection of a debt.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The debt collector states the balance (in a validation notice, demand, call, or credit report).
atoms.effect: The character, amount and legal status of the balance must be true. A balance that includes deductions or charges the state or HUD rule does not allow (e.g. a forfeited deposit, a charge for normal wear and tear, the HAP portion of voucher rent, an SCRA early termination charge) misstates the amount.
atoms.quote:
The false representation of-
(A) the character, amount, or legal status of any debt; or

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The debt collector threatens an action (suit, credit reporting, referral).
atoms.effect: The action must be one that can legally be taken and is intended to be taken. A threat to sue on a time-barred balance, or while an automatic stay is in effect, fails this rule.
atoms.quote: The threat to take any action that cannot legally be taken or that is not intended to be taken.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The debt collector reports or threatens to report the balance to a consumer reporting agency or anyone else.
atoms.effect: It may not communicate credit information it knows or should know is false, and must report a disputed balance as disputed.
judgment_terms: known or which should be known to be false
atoms.quote: Communicating or threatening to communicate to any person credit information which is known or which should be known to be false, including the failure to communicate that a disputed debt is disputed.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: Initial written communication (and the initial oral one, if first contact is oral); every later communication; not formal pleadings.
atoms.effect: The first communication must say the collector is attempting to collect a debt and any information obtained will be used for that purpose; each later communication must say it is from a debt collector (Reg F 1006.18(e); translations must be complete).
atoms.quote: The failure to disclose in the initial written communication with the consumer and, in addition, if the initial communication with the consumer is oral, in that initial oral communication, that the debt collector is attempting to collect a debt and that any information obtained will be used for that purpose, and the failure to disclose in subsequent communications that the communication is from a debt collector, except that this paragraph shall not apply to a formal pleading made in connection with a legal action.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: A debt collector (e.g. a manager or Handoff that is a debt collector) sends collection communications.
atoms.effect: It must use its true business name; it may not collect under the owner's name or another name. A debt collector may use a registered trade or doing-business-as name (Reg F comment 34(c)(2)(i)-1).
atoms.quote: The use of any business, company, or organization name other than the true name of the debt collector's business, company, or organization.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The debt collector collects or tries to collect any amount, including interest, fees, charges or expenses incidental to the principal (late fees, collection fees, payment-processing fees, attorney fees, interest).
atoms.effect: Only amounts expressly authorized by the lease or permitted by law may be collected. State and HUD limits on move-out charges therefore bind the collector's demand; a collection fee not in the lease and not permitted by law cannot be added. Mirrored in Reg F 1006.22(b).
judgment_terms: expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt
atoms.quote: The collection of any amount (including any interest, fee, charge, or expense incidental to the principal obligation) unless such amount is expressly authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The debt collector writes to the consumer by mail.
atoms.effect: No postcards; nothing on the envelope except the collector's address and a business name that does not indicate debt collection (Reg F 1006.22(f)(1)-(2)).
atoms.quote: Using any language or symbol, other than the debt collector's address, on any envelope when communicating with a consumer by use of the mails or by telegram, except that a debt collector may use his business name if such name does not indicate that he is in the debt collection business.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: Initial communication with the consumer in connection with collecting the balance, unless the consumer has paid.
atoms.effect: Within five days (unless included in the initial communication), send a written notice with the amount, the creditor's name, and the 30-day dispute and original-creditor rights. Content, form and timing are fixed by US:12CFR1006.34.
atoms.quote: Within five days after the initial communication with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt, a debt collector shall, unless the following information is contained in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt, send the consumer a written notice containing-

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 2006-10-13 (Pub. L. 109-351 added the last two sentences)
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: The consumer disputes in writing within the 30-day period, or requests the original creditor's name and address.
atoms.effect: Cease collecting the balance (or the disputed part) until verification (or a judgment copy, or the original creditor's name) is mailed. Collection may continue during the 30 days absent a dispute, but may not overshadow the dispute rights. For a move-out balance, verification is the lease terms and the itemized statement that establish each charge (Reg F 1006.38).
atoms.quote: the debt collector shall cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion thereof, until the debt collector obtains verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment, or the name and address of the original creditor, and a copy of such verification or judgment, or name and address of the original creditor, is mailed to the consumer by the debt collector.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector bringing suit (e.g. collection attorney)
atoms.condition: A debt collector sues the former tenant on the balance (not an action to enforce an interest in real property securing the obligation).
atoms.effect: Sue only in the judicial district or similar legal entity where the consumer signed the lease or where the consumer resides when the action begins. The owner suing in its own name is not bound by this section. Mirrored in Reg F 1006.30(d).
judgment_terms: judicial district or similar legal entity
atoms.quote:
(A) in which such consumer signed the contract sued upon; or
(B) in which such consumer resides at the commencement of the action.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: any person (incl. a vendor such as Handoff designing letters for owners)
atoms.condition: A person designs, compiles and furnishes a form knowing it will be used to make the consumer believe someone other than the creditor is participating in the collection, when that person is not in fact participating.
atoms.effect: Unlawful; the person is liable as a debt collector under 1692k. A service that lends its name to owner-sent demand letters without making bona fide collection efforts on the account is liable under 1692j, and the owner becomes a debt collector under the false-name clause; a service that in fact collects is judged under Configurations A-B (US:HANDOFF-config-owner-name-only).
atoms.quote: It is unlawful to design, compile, and furnish any form knowing that such form would be used to create the false belief in a consumer that a person other than the creditor of such consumer is participating in the collection of or in an attempt to collect a debt such consumer allegedly owes such creditor, when in fact such person is not so participating.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: debt collector (a person meeting US:15USC1692a(6) and not excluded)
atoms.condition: A debt collector fails to comply with any provision of the subchapter with respect to a person.
atoms.effect: Liable for actual damages, statutory additional damages up to $1,000 per individual action (class: up to the lesser of $500,000 or 1% of net worth), costs and a reasonable attorney's fee. This is the exposure weighed in the hand-off decision.
judgment_terms: such additional damages as the court may allow

atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28

atoms.condition: The violation was unintentional and resulted from a bona fide error despite procedures reasonably adapted to avoid it.
atoms.effect: No liability if the collector proves this by a preponderance. Reg F 1006.6(d)(3) specifies procedures that qualify for email and text errors.
