atoms.quote: A debt collector may not be held liable in any action brought under this subchapter if the debt collector shows by a preponderance of evidence that the violation was not intentional and resulted from a bona fide error notwithstanding the maintenance of procedures reasonably adapted to avoid any such error.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: A consumer sues on an FDCPA violation.
atoms.effect: The action must be brought within one year from the date the violation occurs, in federal or any competent court.
atoms.quote: within one year from the date on which the violation occurs.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.effective_from: 1978-03-20 (Act effective six months after 1977-09-20); current wording of this provision in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.actor: any person subject to the FDCPA
atoms.condition: State or city debt collection law also applies (e.g. NYC DCWP rules; NY GBL art. 29-H; Virginia law).
atoms.effect: The FDCPA displaces state law only where inconsistent, and a state law giving the consumer greater protection is not inconsistent. The collector must meet both; the stricter rule controls.
atoms.quote: For purposes of this section, a State law is not inconsistent with this subchapter if the protection such law affords any consumer is greater than the protection provided by this subchapter.

atoms.instrument: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692-1692p (Consumer Credit Protection Act title VIII)
atoms.condition: The CFPB has determined that a State subjects a class of collection practices to substantially similar requirements with adequate enforcement.
atoms.effect: That class of practices in that State is exempt from the FDCPA. No exemption exists for New York or Virginia; Maine's (1995) is the only one ever granted (US:15USC1692o-NY-VA-none).
atoms.quote: The Bureau shall by regulation exempt from the requirements of this subchapter any class of debt collection practices within any State if the Bureau determines that under the law of that State that class of debt collection practices is subject to requirements substantially similar to those imposed by this subchapter, and that there is adequate provision for enforcement.

atoms.condition: Any person who is a debt collector under 1006.2(i) (which restates 15 U.S.C. 1692a(6) and its exclusions).
atoms.effect: Regulation F applies to that person. A creditor collecting its own debts in its own name, and a person within an exclusion, are outside Regulation F.
atoms.quote: this part applies to debt collectors, as defined in § 1006.2(i), other than a person excluded from coverage by section 1029(a) of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010

atoms.condition: The debt collected is not related to a consumer financial product or service (12 U.S.C. 5481(5)); an ordinary residential lease is not one (US:12USC5481(15)(A)(ii)).
atoms.effect: The validation notice need not state the creditor as of the itemization date or the CFPB website statement; these become optional disclosures (1006.34(d)(3)(viii)).
judgment_terms: debt related to a consumer financial product or service
atoms.quote: Section 1006.34(c)(2)(iii) and (c)(3)(iv) applies to debt collectors only when they are collecting debt related to a consumer financial product or service as defined in § 1006.2(f).

atoms.instrument: Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010, 12 U.S.C. 5481
atoms.condition: A lease of real property.
atoms.effect: It is a 'financial product or service' only if it is a non-operating, purchase-finance-equivalent lease intended at inception to transfer ownership to the lessee. An ordinary residential tenancy is not, so a former tenant's rent or damage balance is not a debt related to a consumer financial product or service.
atoms.quote: extending or brokering leases of personal or real property that are the functional equivalent of purchase finance arrangements, if-

atoms.condition: The former tenant has died.
atoms.effect: The deceased remains a 'consumer'; the validation notice goes to a named person authorized to act for the estate (comment 34(a)(1)-1).
atoms.quote: Consumer means any natural person, whether living or deceased, obligated or allegedly obligated to pay any debt.

atoms.instrument: Regulation F, 12 CFR part 1006, Supplement I (Official Interpretations; CFPB commentary adopted by notice and comment)
atoms.condition: A person collects debts it owns (including purchased defaulted debts), collects none for another, and has no business whose principal purpose is collection.
atoms.effect: Not a debt collector. Confirms US:CASE-Henson-2017 in the regulation's official interpretation; a landlord collecting its own balance is outside Regulation F on both prongs.
atoms.quote: A person who collects or attempts to collect defaulted debts that the person has purchased, but who does not collect or attempt to collect, directly or indirectly, debts owed or due, or asserted to be owed or due, to another, and who does not have a business the principal purpose of which is the collection of debts, is not a debt collector as defined in § 1006.2(i).

atoms.condition: The debt collector emails the former tenant at an address the creditor (landlord) obtained from the tenant and used for the account, after the creditor sent a notice of the transfer with a 35-day or longer opt-out window that expired without opt-out, and the address is on a public domain not known to be employer-provided.
atoms.effect: The collector's procedures are reasonably adapted to avoid a bona fide third-party-disclosure error (1692k(c)). This is how a manager's or owner's tenant email can pass to a collector at hand-off.
atoms.quote: The date by which the debt collector or the creditor must receive the consumer's request to opt out, which must be at least 35 days after the date the notice is sent;

atoms.condition: The debt collector communicates or attempts to communicate electronically (email, text, portal address).
atoms.effect: Each electronic message must state a reasonable and simple opt-out method, without fees or extra information; after opt-out that address may not be used (1006.14(h)).
atoms.quote: must include in such communication or attempt to communicate a clear and conspicuous statement describing a reasonable and simple method by which the consumer can opt out of further electronic communications or attempts to communicate by the debt collector to that address or telephone number.

atoms.condition: The debt collector telephones a person about a particular debt.
atoms.effect: Presumed compliant with 1692d(5) if it places no more than seven calls within seven consecutive days and none within seven days after a telephone conversation about the debt; exceeding either presumes a violation (rebuttable).
atoms.quote: More than seven times within seven consecutive days; nor

atoms.condition: The collector would email an address it knows is employer-provided, or message via a social media platform.
atoms.effect: No email to a known employer-provided address (unless the consumer used or consented to it with the collector); no social media message viewable by the public or the person's contacts.
atoms.quote: Communicate or attempt to communicate with a person in connection with the collection of a debt through a social media platform if the communication or attempt to communicate is viewable by the general public or the person's social media contacts.

atoms.condition: The statute of limitations under applicable (state) law for suing the former tenant on the balance has expired.
atoms.effect: The debt collector may not sue or threaten to sue (proofs of claim in bankruptcy excepted). The limitations period itself is state law (NY CPLR 213; VA 8.01-246) and is owned by the state files.
atoms.quote: A debt collector must not bring or threaten to bring a legal action against a consumer to collect a time-barred debt.

atoms.condition: The debt collector wants to report the balance to a consumer reporting agency (including a tenant-screening agency).
atoms.effect: It must first speak with the consumer about the debt, or mail/send a message about the debt and wait a reasonable period for a notice of undeliverability (14 consecutive days is reasonable, comment 30(a)(1)-2); if notice of undeliverability arrives, it may not report until it satisfies the rule. No 'passive' reporting.
atoms.quote: Places a letter in the mail or sends an electronic message to the consumer about the debt and waits a reasonable period of time to receive a notice of undeliverability.

atoms.condition: The debt collector knows or should know the balance has been paid, settled, or discharged in bankruptcy.
atoms.effect: It may not sell, transfer for consideration, or place the debt for collection (e.g. a manager that is a debt collector may not place a discharged balance with an agency); it may return it to the owner.
atoms.quote: a debt collector must not sell, transfer for consideration, or place for collection a debt if the debt collector knows or should know that the debt has been paid or settled or discharged in bankruptcy.

atoms.condition: Initial communication about the balance (the first time the collector conveys information about it to the consumer, excluding formal pleadings).
atoms.effect: Provide the validation information either in a validation notice sent in the initial communication or within five days after it (delivered per 1006.42), or orally in the initial communication. Not required if the consumer pays before the five-day notice would be due.
atoms.quote:
By sending the consumer a validation notice in the manner required by § 1006.42:
(A) In the initial communication, as defined in paragraph (b)(2) of this section; or
(B) Within five days of that initial communication; or

atoms.condition: The collector itemizes the former tenant's balance.
atoms.effect: It picks one reference date for which it can ascertain the amount: last statement date (last written account statement or invoice from the creditor, which can include the landlord's itemized move-out statement or its service provider's), charge-off date, last payment date, transaction date, or judgment date; and must use that date consistently for that debt. Whether the move-out itemized statement is the 'last statement' is a judgment on the facts.
judgment_terms: written account statement or invoice provided to the consumer by a creditor
atoms.quote: The last statement date, which is the date of the last periodic statement or written account statement or invoice provided to the consumer by a creditor;

atoms.condition: Validation information is provided.
atoms.effect: The validation period runs from providing it to 30 days after the consumer receives or is assumed to receive it; the collector may assume receipt on any date at least five days (excluding federal holidays, Saturdays, Sundays) after providing it. A re-sent notice after a returned one restarts the period.
atoms.quote: For purposes of determining the end of the validation period, the debt collector may assume that a consumer receives the validation information on any date that is at least five days (excluding legal public holidays identified in 5 U.S.C. 6103(a), Saturdays, and Sundays) after the debt collector provides it.

atoms.condition: The collector provides validation information.
atoms.effect: Include: the 1006.18(e) statement; collector's name and dispute mailing address; consumer's name and address; account number if any; current creditor (the owner); itemization date; amount on that date; itemization of interest, fees, payments and credits since then (all fields shown, zeros allowed); current amount; the validation-period end date with dispute, original-creditor and assumed-valid statements; electronic dispute method if sent electronically; the consumer-response section.
atoms.quote:
(v) The name of the creditor to whom the debt currently is owed.
(vi) The itemization date.
(vii) The amount of the debt on the itemization date.
(viii) An itemization of the current amount of the debt reflecting interest, fees, payments, and credits since the itemization date.

atoms.instrument: Regulation F, 12 CFR part 1006, Supplement I (Official Interpretations; CFPB commentary adopted by notice and comment)
atoms.condition: Other applicable law (e.g. NYC's SHIELD Rule from 2027-01-01) requires its own itemization with the validation information.
atoms.effect: The collector may give that itemization instead, if substantially similar to Model Form B-1's.
atoms.quote: If a debt collector is required by other applicable law to provide an itemization of the current amount of the debt with the validation information, the debt collector may comply with § 1006.34(c)(2)(viii) by disclosing the itemization required by other applicable law in lieu of the itemization described in § 1006.34(c)(2)(viii), if the itemization required by other applicable law is substantially similar to the itemization that appears on Model Form B-1 in appendix B to this part.

atoms.condition: The collector uses Model Form B-1 (appendix B), optionally with permitted optional disclosures or substantially similar changes.
atoms.effect: It complies with the content and form requirements and does not thereby overshadow the dispute rights.
atoms.quote: A debt collector who uses Model Form B-1 complies with the information and form requirements of paragraphs (c) and (d)(1) of this section

atoms.condition: During the validation period.
atoms.effect: No collection activity or communication that overshadows or is inconsistent with the dispute and original-creditor rights (e.g. a demand to pay in full within ten days or be sued).
atoms.quote: During the validation period, a debt collector must not engage in any collection activities or communications that overshadow or are inconsistent with the disclosure of the consumer's rights to dispute the debt and to request the name and address of the original creditor.

atoms.condition: The consumer disputes in writing within the validation period (writing includes the response form, mail, or an email address or portal the collector accepts, comment 38-1).
atoms.effect: Cease collecting the debt or disputed portion until it sends verification or a judgment copy (in writing or electronically per 1006.42), or for a duplicative dispute, a notice that it is duplicative. Any report of the balance to a consumer reporting agency must show it as disputed (1692e(8)).
atoms.quote: Upon receipt of a dispute submitted by the consumer in writing within the validation period, a debt collector must cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion of the debt, until the debt collector:

atoms.condition: The collector sends a required disclosure (validation notice, verification) in writing or electronically to a former tenant.
atoms.effect: Send it in a manner reasonably expected to give actual notice and in a form the consumer can keep. Mailing to the last known address is a safe harbor unless the collector knows or should know the consumer no longer lives or receives mail there; so mailing to the vacated unit, when the collector knows the tenant moved out, is not within the safe harbor. A returned notice is not delivery.
judgment_terms: reasonably expected to provide actual notice
atoms.quote: a debt collector satisfies § 1006.42(a)(1) if the debt collector mails a printed copy of a disclosure to the consumer's last known address, unless the debt collector, at the time of mailing, knows or should know that the consumer does not currently reside at, or receive mail at, that location.

atoms.condition: The validation notice is sent electronically after the initial communication, or verification or original-creditor information is sent electronically.
atoms.effect: The E-SIGN Act consumer-consent procedure (15 U.S.C. 7001(c)) must be followed.
atoms.quote: must do so in accordance with section 101(c) of the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (E-SIGN Act) (15 U.S.C. 7001(c)).

atoms.condition: The collector begins collection activity on a debt.
atoms.effect: Keep records evidencing compliance from then until three years after the last collection activity on the debt; call recordings, if made, for three years after the call.
atoms.quote: a debt collector must retain records that are evidence of compliance or noncompliance with the FDCPA and this part starting on the date that the debt collector begins collection activity on a debt until three years after the debt collector's last collection activity on the debt.

atoms.instrument: Henson v. Santander Consumer USA Inc., 582 U.S. 79 (2017) (U.S. Supreme Court)
atoms.condition: Deciding whether a person 'regularly collects ... debts owed or due ... another' under 1692a(6).
atoms.effect: The test is whether the person collects for its own account or for another at the time of collection; how the owner came to own the debt does not matter. A landlord (or a successor owner or debt buyer) collecting its own balance is outside that clause. The Court did not decide the 'principal purpose' clause or a person that also collects for others.
atoms.quote:
All that matters is whether the
target of the lawsuit regularly seeks to collect debts for its
own account or does so for “another.”

atoms.instrument: Romea v. Heiberger & Associates, 163 F.3d 111 (2d Cir. 1998)
atoms.actor: court (binding in the Second Circuit: New York)
atoms.condition: Deciding whether a residential tenant's unpaid rent is a 'debt' under 1692a(5).
atoms.effect: Back rent is a debt; it arises from the lease transaction even though no credit was extended. Also held a rent demand letter sent to induce payment is a debt-collection communication. Binds federal courts in New York; in Virginia the Fourth Circuit's Mabe test yields the same result for rent and all other lease charges (US:15USC1692a(5)-lease-charges).
atoms.quote: We therefore hold that, under the FDCPA, back rent is debt.

atoms.condition: Deciding whether the tenant is a servicemember in military service.
atoms.effect: 'Servicemember' is a member of the uniformed services; 'military service' for Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force and Coast Guard is active duty (plus certain National Guard federal-emergency service), and for PHS and NOAA officers active service, including absence for sickness, wounds, leave or other lawful cause.
atoms.quote: The term "servicemember" means a member of the uniformed services, as that term is defined in section 101(a)(5) of title 10.

atoms.condition: Deciding whose lease obligations end with the servicemember's termination (3955(a)(2)).
atoms.effect: 'Dependent' is the spouse, a child (38 U.S.C. 101(4)), or an individual for whom the servicemember provided over half of support for the 180 days before applying for relief.
atoms.quote: an individual for whom the servicemember provided more than one-half of the individual's support for 180 days immediately preceding an application for relief under this chapter.

atoms.condition: A reserve-component member (or Space Force member, (c)) receives an order to report for military service.
atoms.effect: SCRA subchapters I-III, including 3955 lease termination, protect the member from receipt of the order until reporting (or revocation).
atoms.quote: A member of a reserve component who is ordered to report for military service is entitled to the rights and protections of this subchapter and subchapters II and III during the period beginning on the date of the member's receipt of the order

atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28; subsection text as amended through Pub. L. 116-315 (2021-01-05)
atoms.condition: The lease is a covered lease of premises (3955(b)(1)).
atoms.effect: The lessee may terminate the lease at any time after entering military service, after the date of qualifying military orders, or after a qualifying stop-movement order. The landlord cannot refuse.
atoms.quote: The lessee on a lease described in subsection (b) may, at the lessee's option, terminate the lease at any time after-

atoms.condition: The servicemember terminates a joint lease under 3955.
atoms.effect: Any obligation of the servicemember's dependents under the lease ends too. Co-tenants who are not dependents are released as well, because the lease itself terminates as to all parties (US:50USC3955(a)(1)-all-parties).
atoms.quote: A lessee's termination of a lease pursuant to this subsection shall terminate any obligation a dependent of the lessee may have under the lease.

atoms.condition: The lessee died in military service (or covered Guard/Reserve duty), or incurred a catastrophic injury or illness during service.
atoms.effect: The spouse or dependent (or the injured lessee, or for an incapacitated lessee the spouse or dependent) may terminate the lease within one year of the death or injury.
judgment_terms: lacks the mental capacity to contract
atoms.quote: The spouse or dependent of the lessee on a lease described in subsection (b) may terminate the lease during the one-year period beginning on the date of the death of the lessee

atoms.effective_from: 2020-08-14 ((C) added by Pub. L. 116-158, applies to stop-movement orders from 2020-03-01)
atoms.condition: A lease of premises occupied or intended to be occupied by a servicemember or dependents for a residential (or similar) purpose.
atoms.effect: Covered if: (A) signed before the lessee entered military service; (B) signed in service and followed by orders for a permanent change of station (including separation or retirement, 3955(i)(3)) or deployment of 90 days or more; or (C) signed on such orders and followed by a stop-movement order of 30 days or more or indefinite that prevents occupancy.
atoms.quote: the servicemember, while in military service, executes the lease and thereafter receives military orders for a permanent change of station or to deploy with a military unit, or as an individual in support of a military operation, for a period of not less than 90 days; or

atoms.effective_from: 2021-01-05 ((c)(2)(D) applies to notices delivered on or after that date)
atoms.actor: servicemember tenant; landlord or managing agent (recipient)
atoms.condition: The lessee terminates under 3955(a).
atoms.effect: Termination is made by delivering written notice plus a copy of the military orders to the lessor or its agent: by hand, private business carrier, return-receipt mail addressed as the lessor designates, or electronic means (to a designated electronic address, a shared portal, or other means reasonably calculated to ensure actual receipt). Delivery to the managing agent suffices.
judgment_terms: other electronic means reasonably calculated to ensure actual receipt
atoms.cross_time: Electronic delivery (c)(2)(D) applies only to notices delivered on or after 2021-01-05.
atoms.quote: by delivery by the lessee of written notice of such termination, and a copy of the servicemember's military orders, to the lessor (or the lessor's grantee), or to the lessor's agent (or the agent's grantee); and

atoms.condition: A covered lease under (b)(1)(A) or (B) is terminated by notice.
atoms.effect: Monthly-rent lease: termination is effective 30 days after the first date on which the next rent payment is due after the notice is delivered. Any other lease: the last day of the month following the month of delivery. This date ends rent liability and anchors the 30-day prepaid-rent refund.
atoms.quote: termination of the lease under subsection (a) is effective 30 days after the first date on which the next rental payment is due and payable after the date on which the notice under subsection (c) is delivered.

atoms.condition: A lease covered by (b)(1)(C) (stop-movement) is terminated.
atoms.effect: Termination is effective on the date the notice-and-orders requirements of (c) are met.
atoms.quote: In the case of a lease described in subsection (b)(1)(C), termination of the lease under subsection (a) is effective on the date on which the requirements of subsection (c) are met for such termination.

atoms.condition: Rent is unpaid for the period before the effective termination date.
atoms.effect: It is owed on a prorated basis up to the effective date; no rent accrues after it.
atoms.quote: Rent amounts for a lease described in subsection (b)(1) that are unpaid for the period preceding the effective date of the lease termination shall be paid on a prorated basis.

atoms.condition: The lessee terminates under 3955.
atoms.effect: The landlord may not impose an early termination charge (no fee, liquidated damages, lost-rent or re-letting charge for ending early).
atoms.quote: The lessor may not impose an early termination charge

atoms.condition: The lessee terminates under 3955 and, at termination, owes lease obligations other than an early termination charge.
atoms.effect: Taxes, summonses and other lease obligations due and unpaid at termination, including reasonable charges for excess wear, remain payable and may be deducted or collected under state law.
judgment_terms: in accordance with the terms of the lease
atoms.quote: but any taxes, summonses, or other obligations and liabilities of the lessee in accordance with the terms of the lease, including reasonable charges to the lessee for excess wear, that are due and unpaid at the time of termination of the lease shall be paid by the lessee.

atoms.condition: Rent was paid in advance for a period after the effective termination date.
atoms.effect: Refund it to the lessee within 30 days of the effective termination date. The SCRA sets no separate security-deposit refund duty or deadline; the deposit is returned under State law on the State clock (New York: 14 days from vacating, US:50USC3955-deposit-clock-NY; Virginia: 45 days from the later of the effective termination date and vacating, US:50USC3955-deposit-clock-VA), and holding it for post-termination rent is a crime (3955(h)).
atoms.quote: Rents or lease amounts paid in advance for a period after the effective date of the termination of the lease shall be refunded to the lessee by the lessor (or the lessor's assignee or the assignee's agent) within 30 days of the effective date of the termination of the lease.

atoms.condition: The lessor applies to a court before the termination date stated in the notice.
atoms.effect: The court may modify the servicemember's relief as justice and equity require. Absent such an application, the statutory relief stands.
atoms.quote: Upon application by the lessor to a court before the termination date provided in the written notice, relief granted by this section to a servicemember may be modified as justice and equity require.

atoms.condition: A servicemember or dependent lawfully terminated a covered lease, and a person knowingly seizes, holds or detains the security deposit, personal effects or other property (or interferes with removal) to subject it to a claim for rent accruing after the termination date.
atoms.effect: Misdemeanor: fine under title 18, up to one year imprisonment, or both. The deposit may not be applied to rent for any period after the effective termination date.
atoms.quote: Any person who knowingly seizes, holds, or detains the personal effects, security deposit, or other property of a servicemember or a servicemember's dependent who lawfully terminates a lease covered by this section

atoms.condition: Checking the orders delivered with the notice.
atoms.effect: 'Military orders' include official orders (including separation or retirement orders) or any notification, certification or verification from the commanding officer about current or future duty status; 'permanent change of station' includes separation or retirement.
atoms.quote: The term "military orders", with respect to a servicemember, means official military orders (including orders for separation or retirement), or any notification, certification, or verification from the servicemember's commanding officer, with respect to the servicemember's current or future military duty status.

atoms.condition: The landlord relies on a waiver of SCRA rights for the modification or termination of the lease, or retention of property.
atoms.effect: The waiver is effective only if in writing, executed as an instrument separate from the lease, made during or after military service, naming the instrument, and (in a contract) in at least 12-point type. A lease clause waiving 3955 is not effective.
atoms.quote: Any such waiver that applies to an action listed in subsection (b) of this section is effective only if it is in writing and is executed as an instrument separate from the obligation or liability to which it applies.

atoms.actor: landlord or its attorney/agency suing on the balance
atoms.condition: The landlord (or collector) sues a former tenant for the balance and the defendant does not appear.
atoms.effect: Before default judgment, the plaintiff must file an affidavit (or declaration under penalty of perjury) stating whether the defendant is in military service with supporting facts, or that it cannot determine; a knowingly false affidavit is a crime. If the defendant is in service, the court appoints counsel first and may stay 90 days.
atoms.quote: the court, before entering judgment for the plaintiff, shall require the plaintiff to file with the court an affidavit-

atoms.condition: During the servicemember's military service, for premises occupied primarily as a residence with monthly rent at or below the annual threshold (US:FR-2026-04689).
atoms.effect: Except by court order, the landlord may not subject the premises to a distress (seizing the tenant's goods to satisfy rent). Knowing participation is a misdemeanor. In Virginia, statutory distress is a live remedy and needs a court order for a covered servicemember (US:50USC3951-distress-VA); New York abolished distress in 1846 (US:50USC3951-distress-NY).
judgment_terms: occupied or intended to be occupied primarily as a residence
atoms.quote: subject such premises to a distress during the period of military service.

atoms.instrument: Department of Defense notice, 91 FR 11527 (2026-03-10), under 50 U.S.C. 3951(a)(2)-(3)
atoms.condition: Applying 3951(a)(1) in calendar year 2026.
atoms.effect: The maximum monthly rent for 3951 protection is $10,542.60.
atoms.quote: the maximum monthly rental amount calculated as of January 1, 2026, is $10,542.60.

atoms.condition: The landlord holds a lien (for storage, cleaning, or any other reason) on a servicemember's property or effects, during service or within 90 days after.
atoms.effect: It may not foreclose or enforce the lien without a court order obtained first; a knowing violation is a misdemeanor. Holding or selling a servicemember's belongings left at move-out and applying them to unpaid amounts enforces a lien; disposing of abandoned property without sale or application does not (US:50USC3958-lien-enforcement).
atoms.quote: A person holding a lien on the property or effects of a servicemember may not, during any period of military service of the servicemember and for 90 days thereafter, foreclose or enforce any lien on such property or effects without a court order granted before foreclosure or enforcement.

atoms.condition: A person violates the SCRA (e.g. charges an early termination fee, withholds prepaid rent beyond 30 days).
atoms.effect: The aggrieved person may sue for equitable relief and monetary damages, including as a class notwithstanding any prior agreement, and may recover costs and a reasonable attorney fee. The Attorney General may also sue, with civil penalties up to $55,000 for a first violation and $110,000 for a later one (US:50USC4041-ag-penalties), and these remedies add to consequential and punitive damages under other law (US:50USC4043-other-remedies).
atoms.quote: Any person aggrieved by a violation of this chapter may in a civil action-

construction.quote: Nothing in section 4041 or 4042 of this title shall be construed to preclude or limit any remedy otherwise available under other law, including consequential and punitive damages.

atoms.reasoning: Section 4041 sets the Attorney General's remedies and penalties, and 4043 preserves remedies under other law.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 982 (Section 8 Tenant-Based Assistance: Housing Choice Voucher Program)
atoms.effective_from: in force on 2026-09-28 (unchanged in eCFR point-in-time since 2017)
atoms.condition: An HCV-assisted tenant moves out.
atoms.effect: Subject to state or local law and the lease, the owner may apply the deposit and any interest on it to unpaid rent payable by the tenant, damages to the unit, or other amounts the tenant owes under the lease. 'Rent payable by the tenant' is the tenant's share only (US:24CFR982.451(b)(4)).
judgment_terms: other amounts the tenant owes under the lease
atoms.quote: When the tenant moves out of the dwelling unit, the owner, subject to State or local law, may use the security deposit, including any interest on the deposit, in accordance with the lease, as reimbursement for any unpaid rent payable by the tenant, damages to the unit or for other amounts the tenant owes under the lease.

atoms.condition: The owner has charged items against the deposit of an HCV tenant who moved out.
atoms.effect: Give the tenant a written list of every item charged and its amount, and promptly refund the unused balance. 'Promptly' means without delay once the charges are determined and never later than the State deadline (New York 14 days; Virginia 45 days); a refund within the State deadline satisfies it (US:24CFR982.313(d)-promptly).
atoms.quote: The owner must give the tenant a written list of all items charged against the security deposit, and the amount of each item. After deducting the amount, if any, used to reimburse the owner, the owner must refund promptly the full amount of the unused balance to the tenant.

atoms.condition: The deposit does not cover what the HCV tenant owes under the lease.
atoms.effect: The owner may seek to collect the balance from the tenant. There is no PHA or HUD reimbursement route in the voucher program.
atoms.quote: If the security deposit is not sufficient to cover amounts the tenant owes under the lease, the owner may seek to collect the balance from the tenant.

atoms.condition: The HCV family moves out.
atoms.effect: The owner keeps the housing assistance payment for the move-out month; the PHA pays nothing for later months. Rent for later months (e.g. under a lease term or notice period) can be claimed only against the tenant's own share, never as the lost HAP.
atoms.quote: If the family moves out of the unit, the PHA may not make any housing assistance payment to the owner for any month after the month when the family moves out. The owner may keep the housing assistance payment for the month when the family moves out of the unit.

atoms.condition: Stating or collecting rent owed by an HCV tenant, including at move-out.
atoms.effect: The owner may not demand or accept rent from the tenant above the tenant's share (rent to owner minus HAP) and must return any excess; the family is not responsible for the HAP portion. A move-out balance may not include HAP the PHA did not pay.
atoms.quote: The family is not responsible for payment of the portion of rent to owner covered by the housing assistance payment under the HAP contract between the owner and the PHA.

atoms.condition: HCV tenancy.
atoms.effect: Collecting the deposit, the tenant contribution, and charges for unit damage by the family is the owner's responsibility, not the PHA's.
atoms.quote:
Collecting from the family:
(i) Any security deposit.
(ii) The tenant contribution (the part of rent to owner not covered by the housing assistance payment).
(iii) Any charges for unit damage by the family.

atoms.condition: A PBV-assisted tenant moves out of the contract unit.
atoms.effect: Same rule as HCV: subject to State and local law and the lease, apply the deposit and interest to unpaid tenant rent, damages or other lease amounts; give a written list of each item and amount; promptly refund the balance (US:24CFR982.313(d)-promptly); the owner may collect a shortfall from the tenant, and the PHA has no liability for it.
atoms.quote: The owner must give the tenant a written list of all items charged against the security deposit and the amount of each item. After deducting the amount used to reimburse the owner, the owner must promptly refund the full amount of the balance to the tenant.

atoms.condition: A PBV family moves out.
atoms.effect: The owner keeps the HAP for the move-out month unless the PHA finds the vacancy is the owner's fault. Any PHA vacancy payment for up to two further months is reduced by rent received, including amounts available from the tenant's security deposit.
judgment_terms: the vacancy is the owner's fault
atoms.quote: cannot exceed the monthly rent to owner under the assisted lease, minus any portion of the rental payment received by the owner (including amounts available from the tenant's security deposit).

atoms.condition: Stating or collecting rent or other amounts from a PBV family.
atoms.effect: The owner may not demand rent above the PHA-determined tenant rent; the family is not responsible for the HAP portion; the PHA pays nothing for damage or other amounts the family owes.
atoms.quote: The PHA may not make any payment to the owner for any damage to the unit, or for any other amount owed by a family under the family's lease or otherwise.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 966 (Public Housing Lease and Grievance Procedure)
atoms.condition: Public housing tenancy.
atoms.effect: The lease must provide for charges for maintenance and repair beyond normal wear and tear and for excess utility consumption, and state the basis (e.g. a posted schedule). Excess-utility charges only if check-metered or from major tenant-supplied appliances. Charges outside this basis are not lease charges.
atoms.quote: The lease shall provide for charges to the tenant for maintenance and repair beyond normal wear and tear and for consumption of excess utilities. The lease shall state the basis for the determination of such charges

atoms.condition: The PHA assesses maintenance/repair, excess-utility or late charges.
atoms.effect: The charges are not due and collectible until two weeks after the PHA gives written notice; the notice is a notice of adverse action, must state the specific grounds and, for a person who is still a tenant, the right to a grievance hearing, and the PHA may not act until the grievance time or process ends. The two-week rule applies to charges assessed after move-out as well (US:24CFR966.4(b)(4)-after-vacating). A move-out charge cannot be demanded, deducted as due, or handed off before then. A PHA must report a former participant's unpaid balance to EIV whether it pursues or writes it off (US:24CFR5.233-debts-owed-PHA).
atoms.quote: The lease shall provide that charges assessed under paragraph (b) (2) and (3) of this section shall not be due and collectible until two weeks after the PHA gives written notice of the charges. Such notice constitutes a notice of adverse action

atoms.condition: The PHA lease provides for a security deposit.
atoms.effect: Capped at one month's rent or a reasonable fixed amount; subject to applicable (state) law, interest earned may be refunded to the tenant on vacating or used for tenant services. Refund and itemization duties otherwise come from state law, which applies except where inconsistent (VA 55.1-1201(A)).
atoms.quote: Subject to applicable laws, interest earned on security deposits may be refunded to the tenant on vacation of the dwelling unit or used for tenant services or activities.

atoms.condition: Damage to the unit or project caused by the tenant, a household member or a guest.
atoms.effect: The tenant must pay reasonable repair charges, other than for wear and tear.
atoms.quote: To pay reasonable charges (other than for wear and tear) for the repair of damages to the dwelling unit, or to the project (including damages to project buildings, facilities or common areas) caused by the tenant, a member of the household or a guest.

atoms.condition: The tenant vacates the unit.
atoms.effect: The PHA must inspect the unit at vacating and give the tenant a statement of any charges under 966.4(b)(2); the tenant may participate in the inspection unless the tenant vacated without notice. The signed move-in condition statement is the baseline.
atoms.quote: The PHA shall be further obligated to inspect the unit at the time the tenant vacates the unit and to furnish the tenant a statement of any charges to be made in accordance with paragraph (b)(2) of this section. Provision shall be made for the tenant's participation in the latter inspection, unless the tenant vacates without notice to the PHA.

atoms.condition: The PHA gives the tenant a notice (e.g. the statement of charges).
atoms.effect: In writing, delivered to the tenant or an adult household member in the dwelling, or sent by prepaid first-class mail properly addressed. After vacating, first-class mail to a proper address is the available route.
atoms.quote: notice to a tenant shall be in writing and delivered to the tenant or to an adult member of the tenant's household residing in the dwelling or sent by prepaid first-class mail properly addressed to the tenant; and

atoms.condition: A dispute about the tenant's or PHA's lease obligations (e.g. move-out charges).
atoms.effect: Resolved under the PHA grievance procedure (24 CFR part 966 subpart B) while the person is a tenant. A person who has vacated has no grievance right for charges first noticed after vacating; a grievance timely requested before vacating runs to completion (US:24CFR966.53(f)-former-tenant).
atoms.quote: The lease must provide that all disputes concerning the obligations of the tenant or the PHA must (except as provided in § 966.51(a)(2)) be resolved in accordance with the PHA grievance procedures.

atoms.condition: Deciding whether a move-out charge dispute is a grievance.
atoms.effect: A grievance is a tenant's dispute about PHA action under the lease that adversely affects the tenant; 'tenant' is defined as an adult who resides in the unit. A former tenant who has moved out is outside the definition (US:24CFR966.53(f)-former-tenant).
atoms.quote: Grievance shall mean any dispute which a tenant may have with respect to PHA action or failure to act in accordance with the individual tenant's lease or PHA regulations which adversely affect the individual tenant's rights, duties, welfare or status.

atoms.condition: The PHA charges for services, repairs or utilities by schedule.
atoms.effect: The schedule must be posted in the project office and furnished on request; changes need 30 days' written notice with a chance to comment. A move-out charge must come from the posted schedule in force.
atoms.quote: Schedules of special charges for services, repairs and utilities and rules and regulations which are required to be incorporated in the lease by reference shall be publicly posted in a conspicuous manner in the Project Office and shall be furnished to applicants and tenants on request.

atoms.condition: Public housing lease terms relied on at move-out.
atoms.effect: Void and prohibited: distraint (holding tenant property as a pledge for charges); holding or selling possessions without notice and a court determination; attorney's fees or legal costs regardless of outcome (fees may be recovered only if the tenant loses).
atoms.quote: Provision that the tenant agrees to pay attorney's fees or other legal costs whenever the landlord decides to take action against the tenant even though the court determines that the tenant prevails in the action.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 960 subpart G (pet ownership in public housing)
atoms.condition: A public housing resident paid a pet deposit.
atoms.effect: The PHA holds it as state or local law requires for pet deposits (or, if none, for security deposits) and follows that law on retention, interest and return at move-out.
atoms.quote: The PHA shall comply with such applicable law as to retention of the deposit, interest, and return of the deposit or portion thereof to the resident, and any other applicable requirements.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 880 (Section 8 New Construction), subpart F
atoms.condition: Section 8 New Construction project (also Substantial Rehabilitation, 881.601, and State Agency, 883.701).
atoms.effect: Deposits are kept in a segregated interest-bearing account equal to all deposits of families in occupancy plus accrued interest; state and local interest laws also apply. Accrued interest is part of the refund.
atoms.quote: The owner must place the security deposits in a segregated, interest-bearing account.

atoms.condition: A family vacates and wants its deposit back.
atoms.effect: To be considered for the refund, it must give the owner a forwarding address or arrange to pick up the refund. Receipt of the forwarding address starts the owner's 30-day clock.
atoms.quote: In order to be considered for the return of the security deposit, a family which vacates its unit will provide the owner with its forwarding address or arrange to pick up the refund.

atoms.condition: The owner receives the vacating family's forwarding address.
atoms.effect: Within 30 days (or a shorter State or local deadline) after receiving the vacating family's forwarding address (from vacating if the address came earlier; US:24CFR880.608(d)-anchor): refund the full deposit plus interest to a family owing nothing; or give a family owing rent or other lease amounts a list itemizing unpaid rent, damages and estimated repair costs, with a statement of the family's rights under State and local law, and refund any unused balance. Rent here is the family contribution only.
atoms.quote: Within 30 days (or shorter time if required by State, or local law) after receiving notification of the family's forwarding address, the owner must:

atoms.condition: The owner does not provide the itemized list.
atoms.effect: The family is entitled to the full deposit plus accrued interest.
atoms.quote: If the owner fails to provide the list, the family will be entitled to the refund of the full amount of the security deposit plus accrued interest.

atoms.condition: The family disagrees with deductions from the deposit.
atoms.effect: The family may present objections at an informal meeting; the owner records disagreements and meetings in the tenant file for the contract administrator. State-law remedies remain.
atoms.quote: In the event a disagreement arises concerning reimbursement of the security deposit, the family will have the right to present objections to the owner in an informal meeting.

atoms.condition: The deposit and interest do not cover unpaid tenant rent or other lease amounts, and the owner gave the family the (d)(2) list.
atoms.effect: The owner may claim reimbursement from the contract administrator (a 'special claim') up to the lesser of the amount owed or one month's contract rent minus the deposit and interest, applied first to unpaid tenant rent; nothing for rent after the tenancy ends. Available under renewed HAP contracts (US:HUD-SpecialClaims-renewal); HUD's procedure requires a certified demand letter and referral to a collection agency before claiming, and filing within 180 days (US:HUD-SpecialClaims-procedure).
atoms.quote: No reimbursement may be claimed for unpaid rent for the period after termination of the tenancy.

atoms.condition: Section 8 Substantial Rehabilitation project.
atoms.effect: Part 880 subpart F, including 880.608, applies.
atoms.quote: All of the provisions of part 880, subpart F, of this chapter apply to projects assisted under this part

atoms.condition: Section 8 State Agency project.
atoms.effect: Part 880 subpart F, including 880.608, applies, with 'contract administrator' read as the state Agency while its ACC is in effect.
atoms.quote: All of the provisions of part 880, subpart F, of this chapter apply to projects assisted under this part, subject to the requirements of § 883.105.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 884 (Section 8 Housing Assistance Program for New Construction set-aside for Section 515 Rural Rental Housing)
atoms.condition: A family vacates a part 884 unit.
atoms.effect: Subject to state and local law, apply the deposit to unpaid rent or other lease amounts; refund the full deposit or unused balance; include interest where state law requires it; claim any shortfall from HUD or the PHA up to the remainder of one month's contract rent, applied first to rent. No federal deadline or itemization duty is stated here; state law supplies them.
atoms.quote: If a Family vacates the unit owing no rent or other amount under the Lease or if such amount is less than the amount of the security deposit, the Owner shall refund the full amount or the unused balance, as the case may be, to the Family.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 886 subpart A (Section 8 Loan Management Set-Aside)
atoms.condition: A family vacates a Loan Management Set-Aside unit.
atoms.effect: Same as 884.115: state-law-subject use of the deposit, refund of the unused balance with any state-law interest, HUD claim up to the remainder of one month's contract rent.
atoms.quote: If the Family has provided a security deposit and it is insufficient for such reimbursement, the Owner may claim reimbursement from HUD, not to exceed an amount equal to the remainder of one month's Contract Rent.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 886 subpart C (Section 8 Property Disposition)
atoms.condition: A family vacates a Property Disposition Set-Aside unit.
atoms.effect: Subject to state and local law, apply the deposit to unpaid family contribution or other lease amounts and refund the unused balance with state-law interest; claim a shortfall from HUD up to the lesser of the amount owed or two months' contract rent, less the greater of the deposit collected or collectible, applied first to unpaid family contribution.
atoms.quote: If a Family vacates the unit, the Owner, subject to State and local law, may use the security deposit as reimbursement for any unpaid Family Contribution or other amount which the Family owes under the Lease.

atoms.condition: A family vacates a Moderate Rehabilitation unit.
atoms.effect: Subject to state and local law, apply the deposit to unpaid tenant rent or other lease amounts and refund the unused balance with state-law interest; claim a shortfall from the PHA up to the lesser of the amount owed or two months' contract rent, less the greater of the deposit collected or collectible; nothing for rent after the family vacates.
atoms.quote: No reimbursement may be claimed for unpaid rent for the period after the Family vacates.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 891 (Section 202 and Section 811 supportive housing)
atoms.condition: A household vacates a Section 202 or 811 assisted unit and provides a forwarding address (or arranges pickup).
atoms.effect: Within 30 days of the notification (or a shorter state/local deadline): refund the full balance to a household owing nothing; or give an itemized list of each amount with a statement of rights under state and local law, and refund any unused balance.
atoms.quote: Within 30 days (or shorter time if required by State or local law) after receiving notification under paragraph (b)(2) of this section, the Owner (or Borrower) must:

atoms.condition: The deposit balance does not cover amounts owed and the (b)(3)(ii) list was given.
atoms.effect: Claim reimbursement from HUD up to the lesser of the amount owed or one month's per-unit operating cost (or contract rent), minus the deposit balance, applied first to unpaid tenant rent; nothing for rent after the tenancy ends.
atoms.quote: No reimbursement may be claimed for any unpaid tenant rent for the period after termination of the tenancy.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 5 subpart C (pet ownership, housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities)
atoms.condition: A tenant in a covered project paid a refundable pet deposit.
atoms.effect: The deposit may be used only for reasonable expenses directly attributable to the pet (repairs, replacements, fumigation, animal care facilities). Unused amounts are refundable; HUD guidance says within a reasonable time (US:HUD-4350.3-6-24E).
judgment_terms: reasonable expenses directly attributable to the presence of the pet
atoms.quote: The project owner or PHA may use the pet deposit only to pay reasonable expenses directly attributable to the presence of the pet in the project

atoms.condition: HOME-assisted unit, including a private unit leased with HOME tenant-based rental assistance (HRA HOME TBRA in NYC), whose lease must meet 92.253 (24 CFR 92.209(g)); the tenant has moved out leaving property, or the owner seeks legal costs.
atoms.effect: The lease may not let the owner take, hold or sell household property without notice and a court decision, except property left after move-out, which the owner may dispose of under state law. The lease may not make the tenant pay attorney's fees or costs if the tenant wins.
atoms.quote: This prohibition, however, does not apply to an agreement by the tenant concerning disposition of personal property remaining in the housing unit after the tenant has moved out of the unit. The owner may dispose of this personal property in accordance with State law;

construction.quote: The tenant must have a lease that complies with the requirements in § 92.253.

(6) A landlord may not terminate the lease or refuse to renew the lease of a household participating in HRA HOME TBRA, except in accordance with Section 92.253(c) of Title 24 of the Code of Federal Regulations.

atoms.reasoning: HOME tenant-based rental assistance is assistance in a private unit, like CityFHEPS, which the aperture keeps; 92.209(g) applies the 92.253 lease protections to TBRA leases, and 68 RCNY 9-06 applies them to HRA's program.

atoms.instrument: HUD Handbook 4350.3 REV-1, Occupancy Requirements of Subsidized Multifamily Housing Programs, ch. 6 (AGENCY GUIDANCE, not regulation)
atoms.effective_from: Change 4 (2013); latest transmittal on hud.gov as of 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: A tenant moves out of a multifamily-assisted property covered by the handbook (Figure 1-1).
atoms.effect: HUD guidance states the 30 days run from the move-out date; the regulation (880.608(d), 891.435(b)(3)) runs them from receipt of the forwarding address of the vacated family. The regulation governs; the handbook date is never later than the regulatory anchor, so an owner meeting it meets both (US:24CFR880.608(d)-anchor).
atoms.quote:
Within 30 days after the move-out date (or shorter time if required by state and/or
local laws), the owner must either:

atoms.condition: A tenant disputes deposit deductions.
atoms.effect: HUD adds that the owner keeps the record of disagreements and meetings for three years.
atoms.quote:
The owner must keep a record of any disagreements and
meetings in the tenant file for a period of three years for inspection by the HUD
Field Office or Contract Administrator.

atoms.condition: Late charges accrued during a multifamily-assisted tenancy.
atoms.effect: Late fees are capped ($5 after a 5-day grace period, then $1 per day; higher only with approval, not over $30 a month; none for 202/811 PRAC and 202/8 and PAC); accrued unpaid late charges may be deducted from the deposit at move-out if state and local law permit.
atoms.quote:
An owner may deduct accrued, unpaid late charges from the tenant’s security
deposit at the time of move-out, if such a deduction is permitted under state and
local laws.

atoms.condition: The tenant paid a pet deposit (elderly/disabled property).
atoms.effect: Return the unused portion within a reasonable time after move-out; assistance animals are exempt from the pet deposit.
atoms.quote:
Owners must return the unused portion of a pet deposit to the tenant within a
reasonable time after the tenant moves from the property or no longer owns or
keeps a household pet in the unit.

atoms.condition: Damage by carelessness, misuse or neglect of the tenant, household or visitor; keys not returned.
atoms.effect: The bill is limited to actual and reasonable repair costs; accrued unpaid damage charges may be deducted from the deposit at move-out where state law permits; a fee per unreturned key may be charged at move-out; no charges for 'bad behavior'. Other charges only with HUD or contract administrator approval and a schedule in the lease or distributed to tenants (6-25 F).
atoms.quote:
The owner's bill is limited to actual and reasonable costs incurred by the
owner for repairing the damages.

atoms.condition: A tenant vacates a multifamily-assisted unit.
atoms.effect: The owner performs a move-out inspection, compares it with the move-in form, and must allow the tenant to attend on request; HUD gives no wear-and-tear criteria (owner discretion).
atoms.quote:
Upon a tenant's request, he/she must be allowed to attend
the move-out inspection conducted by the owner.

atoms.instrument: HUD-90105-a Model Lease for Subsidized Programs (12/2007), HUD-prescribed lease form (contract term, not regulation)
atoms.condition: Lease signed on the HUD model lease (project-based Section 8 and other multifamily programs) and the tenant moves out.
atoms.effect: Refund of the deposit plus stated interest, less unpaid rent, damage not due to normal wear and tear and not on the move-in report, late and returned-check charges, and unreturned-key charges; within the lease's stated days after the tenant moved out, returned possession and gave a new address; with a written list of deductions and an informal meeting on request. The para. 8a condition (refund only after the 30-day notice) cannot forfeit the deposit in New York or Virginia; only State-permitted deductions apply (US:HUD-90105a-8a-state-law). With multiple tenants, the landlord may pay the refund to any tenant named in the lease.
atoms.quote:
The Landlord may pay the refund to
          any Tenant identified in Paragraph 1 of this Agreement.

atoms.instrument: 7 CFR part 3560 (USDA Rural Development Direct Multi-Family Housing, incl. Section 515)
atoms.condition: A tenant moves out of RD multi-family housing.
atoms.effect: Normal wear and tear is an operating expense: no fee and no deposit withholding for it. The borrower may charge the cost of damage or loss caused or allowed by the tenant, including amounts above the deposit. State and local deposit law governs handling, disputes and interest. Unclaimed deposit funds go to the project's general operating account, and State unclaimed-property law still applies to them (US:7CFR3560.204(f)-state-unclaimed). No extra deposit may have been charged for an assistance animal.
judgment_terms: damage or loss caused or allowed by the tenant
atoms.quote: Borrowers must consider expenses due for addressing normal wear and tear as normal operating expenses and must not charge tenants a fee or withhold security deposits to pay for such costs.

atoms.condition: A tenant with a disability made reasonable modifications at the tenant's expense, and the landlord conditioned permission on restoration.
atoms.effect: At move-out the landlord may require restoration of the interior to its prior condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted, where reasonable (not for changes like a widened door that do not affect the next tenant's use). The landlord may not have increased the customary security deposit for the tenant; a negotiated restoration escrow is allowed.
judgment_terms: where it is reasonable to do so
atoms.quote: In the case of a rental, the landlord may, where it is reasonable to do so, condition permission for a modification on the renter agreeing to restore the interior of the premises to the condition that existed before the modification, reasonable wear and tear excepted.

atoms.condition: A rule, policy or fee (e.g. pet fee, pet deposit, pet-cleaning charge) is applied to a tenant with a disability whose assistance animal is a reasonable accommodation.
atoms.effect: Refusing a reasonable accommodation is discrimination. Pet fees, pet rent, pet deposits and pet-based deductions for an assistance animal must be waived when necessary and reasonable (US:42USC3604(f)(3)(B)-animal-fees); HUD program rules bar them outright in public housing, HUD elderly/disabled projects and RD housing (US:24CFR5.303-animal-program-rules); actual damage by the animal is chargeable like any tenant-caused damage (US:42USC3604(f)(3)(B)-animal-damage).
judgment_terms: may be necessary to afford such person equal opportunity
atoms.quote: a refusal to make reasonable accommodations in rules, policies, practices, or services, when such accommodations may be necessary to afford such person equal opportunity to use and enjoy a dwelling; or

atoms.effective_from: 1979-10-01 (Bankruptcy Reform Act of 1978); in force on 2026-09-28
atoms.condition: The former tenant has filed a bankruptcy petition and the balance arose before the filing.
atoms.effect: Any act to collect, assess or recover the balance is stayed: no demand, no validation notice as collection, no hand-off, no suit, no credit reporting as collection pressure, while the stay lasts. The creditor may file a proof of claim.
judgment_terms: any act to collect, assess, or recover
atoms.quote: any act to collect, assess, or recover a claim against the debtor that arose before the commencement of the case under this title;

atoms.condition: The tenant filed bankruptcy before the landlord applied the deposit, and the deposit refund obligation and the landlord's claim both arose before filing.
atoms.effect: Setting off the pre-petition deposit refund against pre-petition charges is stayed. Applying a lease deposit is setoff, not recoupment, in both forums (US:11USC362(a)(7)-deposit-is-setoff); a temporary hold pending a prompt motion for stay relief is not a setoff (US:CASE-Strumpf-hold).
judgment_terms: debt owing to the debtor that arose before the commencement of the case
atoms.quote: the setoff of any debt owing to the debtor that arose before the commencement of the case under this title against any claim against the debtor; and

atoms.condition: The former tenant received a discharge covering the balance.
atoms.effect: Permanently enjoins any action or act to collect, recover or offset the discharged balance as a personal liability; the account must be written off as to the tenant. A debt collector may not place it for collection (US:12CFR1006.30(b)). A violation is civil contempt where there is no fair ground of doubt that the discharge covered the conduct (US:11USC105-discharge-contempt). The discharge does not affect any other entity's liability, so co-tenants and guarantors stay liable (524(e)); an agreement to pay a discharged debt binds only if it meets 524(c) (US:FRBP4008-reaffirmation); the tenant may repay voluntarily (524(f)).
atoms.quote: operates as an injunction against the commencement or continuation of an action, the employment of process, or an act, to collect, recover or offset any such debt as a personal liability of the debtor, whether or not discharge of such debt is waived; and

construction.quote: (e) Except as provided in subsection (a)(3) of this section, discharge of a debt of the debtor does not affect the liability of any other entity on, or the property of any other entity for, such debt. (f) Nothing contained in subsection (c) or (d) of this section prevents a debtor from voluntarily repaying any debt.

atoms.reasoning: Section 105(a) supplies the contempt remedy for the injunction; 524(c), (e) and (f) limit its reach to the debtor's personal liability.

atoms.actor: furnisher (landlord, manager or agency that reports the balance)
atoms.condition: The landlord, manager or collector reports the former tenant's balance to a consumer reporting agency (credit bureau or tenant-screening agency).
atoms.effect: It may not furnish information it knows or has reasonable cause to believe is inaccurate ('reasonable cause' means specific knowledge beyond the consumer's allegation that would give a reasonable person substantial doubts). Enforcement of subsection (a) is by agencies only (1681s-2(c), (d)).
judgment_terms: reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate
atoms.quote: A person shall not furnish any information relating to a consumer to any consumer reporting agency if the person knows or has reasonable cause to believe that the information is inaccurate.

atoms.condition: The former tenant disputes the balance (e.g. deposit deductions) directly with the furnisher.
atoms.effect: It may not furnish the information without notice that the consumer disputes it.
atoms.quote: If the completeness or accuracy of any information furnished by any person to any consumer reporting agency is disputed to such person by a consumer, the person may not furnish the information to any consumer reporting agency without notice that such information is disputed by the consumer.

atoms.condition: The furnisher reports a delinquent account placed for collection or charged off.
atoms.effect: Within 90 days of furnishing, report the date of delinquency: the month and year the delinquency began that immediately preceded the collection or charge-off. That date starts the credit-report aging clock.
atoms.quote: A person who furnishes information to a consumer reporting agency regarding a delinquent account being placed for collection, charged to profit or loss, or subjected to any similar action shall, not later than 90 days after furnishing the information, notify the agency of the date of delinquency on the account

atoms.condition: A consumer reporting agency notifies the furnisher of the consumer's dispute (1681i(a)(2)).
atoms.effect: Investigate, review the agency's information, report results, correct across nationwide agencies, and modify, delete or block unverifiable items, within the agency's reinvestigation period: 30 days from the agency's receipt of the dispute, extended up to 15 days in the cases 1681i allows, and 45 days after a free annual report (US:15USC1681i-furnisher-deadline). Privately enforceable (1681n, 1681o).
atoms.quote: After receiving notice pursuant to section 1681i(a)(2) of this title of a dispute with regard to the completeness or accuracy of any information provided by a person to a consumer reporting agency, the person shall-

construction.quote: before the end of the 30-day period beginning on the date on which the agency receives the notice of the dispute from the consumer or reseller.

atoms.reasoning: Section 1681s-2(b)(2) ties the furnisher's time to the 1681i reinvestigation period.

atoms.condition: A violation of 1681s-2(a).
atoms.effect: No private civil liability under 1681n/1681o; enforced by federal and state officials only. Violations of (b) remain privately actionable.
atoms.quote: sections 1681n and 1681o of this title do not apply to any violation of-

atoms.instrument: Regulation V, 12 CFR part 1022 subpart E
atoms.condition: The landlord, manager or agency furnishes former-tenant balance information to a consumer reporting agency.
atoms.effect: It must have reasonable written accuracy and integrity policies suited to its size and activity, considering appendix E guidelines.
atoms.quote: Each furnisher must establish and implement reasonable written policies and procedures regarding the accuracy and integrity of the information relating to consumers that it furnishes to a consumer reporting agency.

atoms.instrument: Regulation V, 12 CFR part 1022 subpart E
atoms.condition: The former tenant sends a direct dispute to the furnisher's specified address (or a mailing address on the report) about liability for the balance, its terms, or payment status.
atoms.effect: Conduct a reasonable investigation and report results to the consumer within the time the FCRA gives consumer reporting agencies, unless an exception (e.g. frivolous dispute) applies.

Branches: (1) the landlord holds a lien on it, by statute or by lease (Virginia: the landlord's lien on the tenant's goods recognized in 8.01-130.6 and 8.01-130.9 and preserved by 55.1-1254), and holds, sells or applies the goods or their proceeds to rent or other charges; (2) Virginia 55.1-1254 disposal where the landlord sells the property and applies the proceeds to amounts the tenant owes; (3) the landlord disposes of property deemed abandoned without selling it and without holding it for payment (discard or donation after the required notice).
atoms.effect: (1) and (2) enforce a lien: a court order must be obtained first; the court may stay or adjust; a knowing violation is a misdemeanor. (3) enforces no lien and is governed by State abandoned-property law alone. Separately, if the lease was terminated under 3955, holding the servicemember's effects or deposit for rent accruing after termination is a misdemeanor under 3955(h).
atoms.quote: the term "lien" includes a lien for storage, repair, or cleaning of the property or effects of a servicemember or a lien on such property or effects for any other reason.

construction.quote: Nothing in this section shall affect the right of a landlord to enforce an inchoate or perfected lien of the landlord on the personal property of a tenant
the landlord shall pay such funds to the account of the tenant and apply the funds to any amounts due the landlord by the tenant

A person holding a lien on the property or effects of a servicemember may not, during any period of military service of the servicemember and for 90 days thereafter, foreclose or enforce any lien on such property or effects without a court order granted before foreclosure or enforcement.

atoms.reasoning: 3958 defines lien to include a charge on the property 'for any other reason', so any right to hold or sell goods and apply the value to the tenant's debt is a lien. Virginia's sale-and-apply rule in 55.1-1254 makes the goods answer for the debt, which is lien enforcement; plain disposal of abandoned goods satisfies no debt from them.

atoms.instrument: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3901-4043; N.Y. Gen. Oblig. Law 7-108(1-a)(e), 7-107(6)

Only the State-listed categories may be retained (non-payment of rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear, utilities payable to the landlord, moving and storage). The deposit may not be held for rent accruing after the effective termination date (3955(h)). Prepaid rent for any period after that date is refunded within 30 days of it (3955(f)).

construction.quote: Within fourteen days after the tenant has vacated the premises
for the purpose of subjecting or attempting to subject any of such property to a claim for rent accruing subsequent to the date of termination of such lease

atoms.reasoning: The SCRA sets no deposit deadline and does not move State deadlines; New York's text keys the deadline to vacating only. The SCRA effective date fixes how much rent is owed, which State law then allows the landlord to retain for non-payment.

atoms.instrument: Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, 50 U.S.C. 3901-4043; Code of Virginia 55.1-1226(A), 55.1-1235
atoms.actor: Virginia landlord of a servicemember who terminated under 3955 or 55.1-1235

atoms.effect: The 45-day itemization and refund run from the effective termination date, because 55.1-1226(A) runs from the later of termination of the tenancy and vacating. If the servicemember vacates after the effective date, the 45 days run from vacating. The deposit may not be held for rent accruing after the effective date (3955(h)).
atoms.quote: within 45 days after the termination date of the tenancy or the date the tenant vacates the dwelling unit, whichever occurs last

construction.quote: termination of the lease under subsection (a) is effective 30 days after the first date on which the next rental payment is due and payable after the date on which the notice under subsection (c) is delivered.

atoms.reasoning: The SCRA fixes when the tenancy terminates; Virginia's deadline is keyed to the later of that date and vacating, so the SCRA date controls when the tenant leaves first.

atoms.instrument: Bankruptcy Code, 11 U.S.C. 362(a)(7), 553(a); In re Sweet N Sour 7th Ave. Corp., 431 B.R. 63 (Bankr. S.D.N.Y. 2010); In re Cole, 104 B.R. 736 (Bankr. D. Md. 1989)
atoms.actor: landlord holding a former tenant's deposit
atoms.condition: The tenant files bankruptcy before the landlord has applied the deposit, and the landlord wants to apply the deposit to rent or charges that arose before the filing. Forum New York: Second Circuit recoupment is limited to a single integrated transaction and narrowly construed (Malinowski); S.D.N.Y. treats a lease deposit as setoff. Forum Virginia: no Fourth Circuit decision; bankruptcy courts in the circuit treat application of a deposit as setoff (Cole), consistent with the national rule the S.D.N.Y. surveyed.
atoms.effect: Applying the deposit is a setoff, not recoupment, and is barred by the automatic stay until the landlord obtains relief from the stay under 362(d). After relief, 553(a) allows setoff only of the pre-petition deposit refund against pre-petition claims; charges arising after the filing cannot be set off against it.
atoms.quote: Because lease security deposits are viewed as creating mutual obligations, setoff and not re-coupment is the proper mechanism for landlords to seek recovery of lease security deposits.

construction.quote: the automatic stay remains in force preventing the Landlord from exercising any right to setoff with respect to the Deposit.
The distinction between set-off and recoupment is crucial because set-off claims are subject to the automatic stay of 11 U.S.C. § 362
Other courts have generally treated the application of security deposits as subject to the rules for setoff under 11 U.S.C. § 553 in bankruptcy cases.

this title does not affect any right of a creditor to offset a mutual debt owing by such creditor to the debtor that arose before the commencement of the case under this title against a claim of such creditor against the debtor that arose before the commencement of the case

atoms.reasoning: A deposit creates two obligations, the tenant's to perform and the landlord's to return the deposit, which is the mutuality that defines setoff; recoupment is confined in the Second Circuit to a single integrated transaction and is narrowly construed. No court in either circuit treats a lease deposit as recoupment, and the only decisions found in each (S.D.N.Y.; D. Md.) treat it as setoff.

atoms.instrument: Citizens Bank of Maryland v. Strumpf, 516 U.S. 16 (1995)
atoms.actor: landlord holding a former tenant's deposit after the tenant files bankruptcy
atoms.condition: The landlord claims a pre-petition setoff right against the deposit refund and promptly moves for relief from the stay.
atoms.effect: The landlord may withhold the disputed part of the refund temporarily while its motion is pending; a temporary refusal to pay, pending relief, is not a setoff and does not violate the stay. The hold is limited to the amount properly subject to setoff; the rest is paid to the payee stated in US:11USC542-refund-payee.
atoms.quote: In our view, petitioner's action was not a setoff within the meaning of §362(a)(7). Petitioner refused to pay its debt, not permanently and absolutely, but only while it sought relief under §362(d) from the automatic stay.

construction.quote: Five days later, petitioner filed in the Bankruptcy Court, under §362(d), a "Motion for Relief from Automatic Stay and for Setoff."

atoms.reasoning: Strumpf treats a hold paired with a prompt stay-relief motion as outside 362(a)(7); a bank account and a deposit refund are both debts owed to the debtor, so the rule applies to the landlord.

atoms.instrument: 24 CFR part 966 subpart B (PHA grievance procedure)
atoms.condition: A person who has vacated a public-housing unit disputes move-out charges first noticed after vacating.
atoms.effect: The person is no longer a 'tenant' (an adult who resides in the unit) and has no right to the PHA grievance procedure for those charges; the dispute goes to the informal channels the PHA offers and to court under State law. A grievance that a tenant timely requested before vacating runs to completion, and the PHA may not act on that charge until it does.

construction.quote: The PHA grievance procedure shall be applicable (except as provided in paragraph (a)(2) of this section) to all individual grievances as defined in § 966.53 of this subpart between the tenant and the PHA.
who resides in the unit and executed the lease as the lessee

the PHA shall not take the proposed action until the time for the tenant to request a grievance hearing has expired, and (if a hearing was timely requested by the tenant) the grievance process has been completed.

atoms.reasoning: The grievance procedure applies to grievances between 'the tenant' and the PHA, and 'tenant' is defined in the present tense by residence; HUD's guidebook restates the residence element. A right that attached while the person was a tenant is not lost by moving out, because 966.4(e)(8)(ii)(B) bars action until a timely requested process ends.

atoms.condition: The PHA assesses maintenance and repair charges (or excess-utility or late charges) against a household that has vacated.
atoms.effect: The lease term still applies: the charges are not due and collectible until two weeks after the PHA's written notice, and the notice must state the specific grounds. The statement of a right to a grievance hearing is required only where the person is still a tenant (charges noticed before move-out). The balance cannot be demanded as due, deducted as due, handed off or reported before the two weeks run.
atoms.quote: shall not be due and collectible until two weeks after the PHA gives written notice of the charges.

construction.quote: To notify the tenant of the specific grounds for any proposed adverse action by the PHA.
When the PHA is required to afford the tenant the opportunity for a hearing under the PHA grievance procedure for a grievance concerning a proposed adverse action:

atoms.reasoning: The two-week rule is a lease term about when charges fall due; it contains no residence condition and binds the PHA as a lease obligation that survives move-out for charges arising under the lease. The hearing notice is conditioned on the PHA being 'required to afford the tenant' a hearing, which it is not for a non-resident.

atoms.condition: A tenant with a disability keeps an animal that is a reasonable accommodation (it performs work, provides assistance or provides disability-related support), and the landlord's pet policy imposes a pet fee, pet rent, pet deposit, or a move-out deduction because an animal was kept.
atoms.effect: The pet fee, pet rent, pet deposit and any deduction charged because the animal was present are rules the landlord must waive when the waiver is necessary to afford equal opportunity to use the dwelling and is reasonable (no undue financial or administrative burden, no fundamental alteration). Refusing is discrimination. HUD's assistance-animal notices FHEO-2013-01 and FHEO-2020-01 were withdrawn effective 2025-09-17 and are not authority; the statute and 24 CFR 100.204 govern and are unchanged.

FHEO 2020-01: Assessing a Person's Request
