servicemember_early_termination_NY.note: NYC tenant on a monthly lease gets PCS orders and emails notice plus orders to the manager's designated address on 2026-10-10 (rent due on the 1st). Effective date: 30 days after 2026-11-01 = 2026-12-01. Rent is owed prorated to that date; no early termination fee; reasonable excess-wear charges remain. Any rent prepaid for after 2026-12-01 is refunded by 2026-12-31. The deposit follows NY GOL 7-108/7-107 (14-day itemized statement after vacating, in NY.json; NY:MIL-310(2) is the state analog). Holding the deposit against December rent is a federal misdemeanor. A lease clause waiving the right is void unless a separate written waiver meets 3918.

servicemember_early_termination_VA.note: Virginia has its own servicemember termination (VA:55.1-1235, in VA.json) with no liquidated damages. The federal rule runs alongside: the tenant may use either, and the landlord must honor the more protective result on each point (no early termination charge; prorated rent; 30-day prepaid-rent refund). Deposit disposition follows 55.1-1226 (45 days). The 45 days run from the effective termination date when the servicemember left earlier. If the servicemember left belongings, levying distress on them or selling them and applying the proceeds to unpaid amounts needs a court order first (3951/3958); plain disposal of abandoned property under 55.1-1254 does not.

hud_voucher_tenant_moves_out_NYC.note: The owner keeps the move-out month's HAP; the PHA pays nothing after. The deposit (and interest, which NY law requires in 6+ unit buildings) may cover the tenant's share of unpaid rent, damage and other lease amounts, subject to NY/NYC law (itemized statement within 14 days; if rent-stabilized, NYC RSC limits). The balance stated to the tenant excludes the HAP portion. Any shortfall is collected from the tenant; no PHA claim exists. A PBV unit (including RAD PBV) follows 983.259, 983.352, 983.353 the same way.

hud_voucher_tenant_moves_out_VA.note: Same federal rule. VA 55.1-1201(A) makes HUD rules control where inconsistent; 982.313 defers to state law, so the 45-day itemization in 55.1-1226 applies, and a refund within those 45 days satisfies 982.313(d)'s 'promptly' (US:24CFR982.313(d)-promptly).

public_housing_tenant_moves_out.note: The PHA inspects at vacating (tenant may join unless left without notice) and sends a statement of charges from the posted schedule (repair beyond normal wear and tear; check-metered excess utilities). Charges are not due until two weeks after written notice, which must name the grounds and grievance right. Deposit handling and refund timing then follow state law (NY/NYC; VA 55.1-1226, with HUD controlling where inconsistent). No distraint or attorney-fees-regardless clauses. NYC public housing (NYCHA) is outside the RSC (NYC:RSC-2520.11(b)).

project_based_section8_tenant_moves_out.note: Refund or itemized list with rights statement within 30 days of the forwarding address (or the state's shorter deadline: NY 14 days after vacating); no list means full refund plus interest; informal meeting on request; shortfall may be claimed from the contract administrator up to one month's contract rent less the deposit. Rent charged is the family contribution only.

manager_hands_balance_to_agency.note: The agency is a debt collector; the owner/manager passing the file to it is communicating with 'the creditor's' collector (allowed; VA:55.1-1209(A)(11) permits the release in Virginia). The amount handed off must contain only charges the lease authorizes and state law permits, because the agency's demand is judged by 1692f(1)/1692e(2)(A). The agency must send a Reg F validation notice (itemization date, e.g. the last written statement from the landlord; itemization; 30-day dispute period), deliver it where the tenant actually receives mail (not the vacated unit if it knows the tenant left), wait out undeliverability before reporting, never sue on a time-barred balance, and stop on a timely dispute until it sends verification. In NYC the agency needs a DCWP licence (NYC:ADC-20-490). If the tenant is in bankruptcy, nothing is handed off; if discharged, the account is written off.

landlord_collects_own_balance.note: An owner collecting its own former tenants' balances in its own name (itself or through its employees) is a creditor, not a debt collector: FDCPA and Reg F do not apply. It becomes one if it uses a name suggesting a third party is collecting. It still faces: state and NYC collection rules (NYC's rules reach creditors; SHIELD from 2027-01-01), FCRA furnisher duties if it reports, the SCRA default-judgment affidavit if it sues, and the bankruptcy stay and discharge.

handoff_collects_for_owner.note: Handoff collects balances owed to owners ('another'). It is not the owner's employee (A) or affiliate (B). Configuration A: engaged on the account before the balance is in default (at lease-up, notice or move-out) - excluded by (F)(iii) for that account, whatever its principal purpose. Configuration B: takes on a defaulted balance - a debt collector if it collects for others regularly (Goldstein factors), and must then use its true name (1692e(14)). Configuration C: owner sends letters under Handoff's name while Handoff makes no bona fide collection efforts - the owner becomes a debt collector and Handoff is liable under 1692j; not so if Handoff really collects or the name was used from the start of the tenancy. Configuration D: if collection is the principal purpose of Handoff's business, it is covered for every non-excluded account. Configuration E: buying balances takes Handoff out of the second clause (Henson) but not the first. A move-out balance defaults when the lease's delinquency period runs or when the owner treats it as in default, not on the due date. Which configuration Handoff adopts is Owen's operating choice. In NYC, the DCWP licence question is owned by NYC.json.

former_tenant_in_bankruptcy.note: After a petition, no collection act on the pre-petition balance; the landlord files a proof of claim. Applying the deposit is a setoff barred by the stay until relief is granted (US:11USC362(a)(7)-deposit-is-setoff); the landlord may hold the disputed amount only while it promptly seeks relief (US:CASE-Strumpf-hold). After discharge, the balance is written off as to the tenant and cannot be placed for collection. The refund is estate property: in chapter 7 it is paid to the trustee (or on the trustee's order) once the landlord knows of the case; in chapter 13 to the debtor (US:11USC542-refund-payee).
